policy: Research supplement originating on 2026-08-13 and independently source-reviewed during integration on 2026-10-20. Dispositions propose design changes; they do not promote sources into the canonical runtime evidence ledger or establish product efficacy. The canonical ledger remains authoritative until a separately reviewed integration.

sources.citation: Marques, M. M., et al. (2023). The Behaviour Change Technique Ontology: Transforming the Behaviour Change Technique Taxonomy v1.
sources.population: Ontology experts, behaviour-change researchers, and intervention reports used for annotation reliability.
sources.intervention: Iterative development and testing of a behaviour change technique ontology.
sources.comparator: BCT Taxonomy v1 and successive ontology drafts.
sources.duration: Multi-stage development; not an intervention follow-up study.
sources.outcomes: The published 2023 ontology described 281 BCTs in 20 groups and annotation reliability; these counts are not an assertion about the current ontology.
sources.result: Supports standardized active-ingredient names and identifiers; does not rank effectiveness.
sources.risk_of_bias: Not an efficacy study; terminology coverage and mappings remain iterative.
sources.limitation: An ontology mapping identifies intervention content but does not establish fit or effect for a user.

sources.citation: NIST AI 600-1. Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile (2024).
sources.population: Organizations designing, developing, deploying, or evaluating generative AI systems.
sources.intervention: Cross-sector risk-management profile and recommended actions.
sources.comparator: NIST AI RMF 1.0 without the generative-AI profile.
sources.outcomes: Governance, measurement, pre-deployment testing, incident disclosure, and risk-management actions.
sources.result: Supports a control crosswalk and explicit residual-risk/evidence status.
sources.risk_of_bias: Voluntary framework; not product certification or outcome evidence.
sources.limitation: The profile does not specify this product's acceptance thresholds or prove that implemented controls work.

sources.citation: International Coaching Federation. ICF Code of Ethics, effective April 1, 2025.
sources.population: ICF professionals and the ICF ecosystem.
sources.comparator: Prior ICF code applicable through March 31, 2025.
sources.outcomes: Current professional expectations for agreements, boundaries, confidentiality, conflicts, and responsibility.
sources.result: Supports updating the governance crosswalk and date-specific ethics references.
sources.risk_of_bias: Professional code, not empirical evidence and not automatically binding on software.
sources.limitation: The product must not imply ICF credentialing, compliance certification, or a human coaching relationship.

sources.citation: Comparing the effectiveness of LLM-powered coaching with human coaching and GPT conversation (2025).
sources.population: 121 people randomized: 49 LLM-coaching, 36 human-coaching, and 36 GPT-conversation assignments; 32 completed (10, 12, and 10 respectively).
sources.comparator: Human coaching and generic GPT-4 conversation.
sources.duration: One 20-minute session with immediate pre/post measures; no delayed product-outcome trial.
sources.outcomes: Self-reported coaching-process ratings, pre/post affect, and qualitative feedback. The paper inconsistently reports ten versus eleven process criteria.
sources.result: Among completers, LLM coaching scored higher than GPT conversation on empathy (p=.02) and encouragement (p=.01); engagement was not significant (p=.10). No detected difference from human coaching does not establish equivalence.
sources.risk_of_bias: High attrition, small completer-only comparisons, subjective ratings, and protocol-specific immediate outcomes limit interpretation and transfer.
sources.limitation: An immediate small-completer result is neither product-efficacy nor human-equivalence evidence; preserve nonsignificant findings and attrition.

sources.citation: A randomised controlled comparison of the effectiveness of human and AI chatbot coaching with goal attainment, wellbeing and self-efficacy (2026).
sources.population: Reported total N=114 across human coaching, AI coaching, and waitlist control in a leadership sample drawn mainly from one corporate organization; the paper has inconsistent control counts (prose 42 versus Table 3 39).
sources.intervention: A hybrid scripted and generative WhatsApp coaching system.
sources.comparator: Accredited human coaching and a waitlist control arm.
sources.duration: Approximately three months, April-July 2024, with four planned weekly one-hour coaching sessions.
sources.outcomes: Goal attainment, motivation, self-efficacy, resilience/hardiness, wellbeing, coaching uptake, and dropout.
sources.result: Human coaching showed broadly stronger improvements than this AI intervention. Not every contrast was significant: the AI self-efficacy difference disappeared after adjustment, and unadjusted hardiness contrasts with the control arm were not significant.
sources.risk_of_bias: Not preregistered; unblinded self-reports, differential coaching uptake, and inconsistent control counts limit interpretation. The leadership sample was drawn mainly from one corporate organization, with additional university recruits.
sources.limitation: Require this product's own delayed outcomes. Do not infer universal AI-coaching ineffectiveness, human superiority on every measure, or efficacy for this product.

sources.citation: Klasnja, P., et al. (2015). Microrandomized Trials: An Experimental Design for Developing Just-in-Time Adaptive Interventions. Health Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/hea0000305
sources.intervention: Repeated randomization of intervention options at decision points.
sources.comparator: Standard parallel trials of integrated intervention packages.
sources.outcomes: Proximal effects and moderation by time or context.
sources.result: Supports estimating proximal component effects and their moderation at repeated decision points, distinct from distal package outcomes. Preregistration is a PGC design requirement, not a reported result of this paper.
sources.risk_of_bias: Designed for optimization research; not suitable for rare events and not automatically ethical or useful for personal coaching.
sources.limitation: Do not randomize support, withhold needed help, or covertly experiment on users; any use requires consent and independent review.

sources.citation: SCRIBE 2016 Statement: Single-Case Reporting Guideline In BEhavioural Interventions.
sources.population: Authors and reviewers of single-case experimental designs in behavioural intervention research.
sources.intervention: A reporting checklist for single-case experimental designs.
sources.outcomes: Completeness and transparency of single-case reports.
sources.result: Supports complete reporting of single-case experiments. Borrowing fields for uncontrolled episode-level pilots is a PGC adaptation, not SCRIBE-compliant causal evidence.
sources.risk_of_bias: Reporting completeness does not remove design bias or create causal identification.
sources.limitation: Reporting completeness does not create experimental control, causal identification, or generalizability from one user.

sources.citation: International Coaching Federation. Artificial Intelligence Coaching Framework and Standards (published November 8, 2024).
sources.population: AI coaching providers, developers, organizations, and coaching stakeholders.
sources.intervention: Six domains: Foundation; Co-Creating the Relationship; Communicating Effectively; Cultivating Learning and Growth; Assurance and Testing; Technical Factors.
sources.outcomes: Governance questions and Basic/Advanced standards for AI coaching.
sources.result: Supports the ICF/NIST control crosswalk and explicit gaps for accessibility, human escalation, privacy, and testing.
sources.risk_of_bias: Professional guidance rather than controlled evidence; several capabilities exceed this alpha.
sources.limitation: Do not claim ICF approval or compliance merely because the crosswalk exists.
